long_biography.plain_text:
Stengos trained as a mechanical engineer at the University of Miami and the National Technical University of Athens. He joined Technical Olympic in 1991, initially managing investment and procurement, then moved through senior roles at construction subsidiary Mochlos. By 2004 he was chief executive of the family-controlled group, whose founder was his father, Konstantinos Stengos.

His mandate has covered Greek construction, American homebuilding, the Porto Carras resort and casino, and marina development. After the group sold Porto Carras and withdrew from public works, Technical Olympic redeployed capital into vessel-owning companies, property projects, marina tourism and renewable energy. Stengos remains chief executive and a significant shareholder, directing that transition from a construction-led conglomerate toward a more diversified investment portfolio.

The authoritative George Stengos form is a supported English rendering. The K. is a patronymic initial rather than sufficient evidence of a conventional middle name, so no middle-name proposal is made.

A SEC filing states that Stengos was 41 on 15 March 2008, which constrains but does not uniquely establish a birth year because the birthday could fall on either side of the calendar boundary. No strong reviewed source supplies an exact day, month, year or birthplace, so those fields remain blank.
